anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved: both outputs prove A/B/C as ancestors in preflight, write the three pre-rework refs, capture evidence then strip/seal before a single non-force home push, edit the body successfully before the close question, render the exact per-target comments with the home URL and bbbbbbb/ccccccc, recheck immediately, close without --delete-branch, and cover every delta including row 5 naming both untouched members. After is slightly cleaner than Before in one respect the author should keep: it introduces G as the post-strip pushed head and runs eligibility against G, whereas Before pushes 'E' (the pre-strip HEAD) and checks ancestry against E, which is internally inconsistent after a strip commit. Two small wording hazards in After: the `Spec: <spec path> at G7` line invents an alias not defined in the alias list (use a short form of G explicitly, e.g. 'G (short SHA)'), and the report puts the seal line after the push line, which is fine but reads out of execution order; keeping the report in execution order (sealed → pushed → body → Closed) would make the ordering fact easier to read off. Otherwise the After wording delivers the change while retaining every fact Before kept.

After's additions (explicit worktree/primary/feature header, literal push command, explicit refs block, 'Selected spec path at the post-seal head', and the 'no supersedes' note) are consistent with the Change and cost nothing. One small wording risk in After is '#14: MEMBER14 newly resolved; retain that refreshed state, not an open-thread claim' — it still attributes correctly and avoids home-history inference, but if you want it unambiguous, name the recorded thread ('src/cap.ts:3 MEMBER14 - newly resolved') so a reader sees the recorded disposition and the refreshed state side by side as Before did. Otherwise keep After as written.
